record.paper_title: Geodesic Nets: Some Examples and Open Problems
record.original_question: Does every closed Riemannian manifold M of dimension at least 3 admit a connected closed geodesic net modelled on the theta graph, namely a finite embedded geodesic net with empty boundary set whose underlying graph has two vertices joined by three distinct edges and whose balancing condition holds at both vertices?

evidence.quote: The corresponding closed geodesic net consists of two vertices connected by 3 distinct geodesics, so that all angles between each pair of geodesics at each of the vertices are equal to 120◦.
Problem 2.0.3. Is it true that each closed Riemannian manifold of dimension ≥ 3 has a θ-graph shaped closed geodesic net?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A geodesic net in a Riemannian manifold $(M,g)$ is a finite graph $\Gamma$ together with a continuous map $f:\Gamma\to M$ such that the image of each edge of $\Gamma$ is a geodesic segment in $M$, and at every vertex $v$ of $\Gamma$ the balancing condition holds: the sum of the unit tangent vectors to the outgoing geodesic edges at $f(v)$ equals zero. A vertex at which only one edge ends is called a boundary vertex; the boundary set is the set of all boundary vertices. A closed geodesic net is one with empty boundary set. The theta graph is the abstract graph with exactly two vertices joined by three distinct edges.

Question: Does every closed (compact, without boundary) Riemannian manifold $M$ of dimension $\ge 3$ admit a connected closed geodesic net modelled on the theta graph, i.e., a geodesic net whose underlying graph is the theta graph (with three geodesic edges between two points of $M$, meeting the balancing condition at both vertices so that consecutive edges make $120^\circ$ angles)?
artifact.status_search_result: The existence of a theta-graph shaped closed geodesic net on every closed Riemannian manifold of dimension at least 3 is listed as an open problem. Related results by Nabutovsky and Rotman provide existence with length bounds under topological hypotheses (e.g., nontrivial second homology), and recent work (2025) discusses generic density of stationary geodesic nets, but no general resolution of this specific question was found.

status_evidence.title: The Minimal Length of a Closed Geodesic Net on a Riemannian Manifold with a Nontrivial Second Homology Group
status_evidence.snippet: On a closed Riemannian manifold with a nontrivial second homology group, there exists a geodesic net of length at most 3 diam(M); it is either a closed geodesic, two loops at a point, or three segments between the same endpoints.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results exist under topological hypotheses but not in full generality.

status_evidence.title: Generic density of stationary geodesic nets that are not closed geodesics
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work on stationary geodesic nets in Riemannian manifolds; theta-graph existence in general remains a recognized question.
status_evidence.claim: Existence questions for geodesic nets of prescribed combinatorial type remain active and the theta-graph case is still posed as open.
